scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the text gives no evidence bearing on the criterion
task: Each entry is a candidate criterion for judging machine-learning conference paper abstracts. Classify each as quality-relevant or incidental.

criteria.name: "Framework" as the contribution noun
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract labels its own contribution a framework, paradigm, pipeline, or scheme rather than naming a concrete object such as an algorithm, model, dataset, bound, or result. Score the choice of noun only.

criteria.name: Leaves a transferable design principle, not only a method
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states a lesson or principle a reader could apply outside this paper's specific method, and separately whether that principle is grounded in the reported results rather than merely suggested; score 0-10 for BOTH together.

criteria.name: Corrects a specific prior claim rather than adding to a pile
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the contribution is positioned as correcting, qualifying, or overturning an identifiable prior claim or widely-held position, as opposed to adding one more method to an existing family. Score low for 'we propose X, which outperforms Y'.

criteria.name: Evaluation conditions match the conditions the claim is about
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge what conditions the abstract's claim is about (a deployment setting, a scale, a data regime), and separately whether the reported evaluation was run under those conditions; score 0-10 for the MATCH. Score low when a claim about practice is supported only by small or idealised experiments.

criteria.name: Necessity established — an ablation shows the components are actually required
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract claims particular components are essential, and separately whether it reports an ablation or controlled comparison establishing that necessity; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for components asserted as key with no ablation, and low for an ablation mentioned with no necessity claim attached.

criteria.name: Poses a specific question and states its answer plainly
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract frames a specific answerable question and then gives the answer in plain terms, rather than describing an area of activity and a contribution to it. Score the question-and-answer structure, not the importance of the question.

criteria.name: Passive-voice density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the abstract is written in the passive voice ('it is shown that', 'experiments were conducted', 'the model is trained') rather than the active voice. Score the grammatical construction only.

criteria.name: Scare-quoted or coined terms in quotation marks
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract puts terms in quotation marks to coin, hedge, or distance itself from them — 'false negatives', 'tabula rasa', 'middle way'. Score the quotation habit only.

criteria.name: Multiplicative speedup notation
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many multiplicative performance figures the abstract states — '3.04x', '91 times', '5 to 10 times faster', 'orders of magnitude'. Count the notation only; do not judge whether the speedup is real, fairly measured, or worth its cost.

criteria.name: Bare mention of the word "ablation"
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract uses the word ablation or ablation study. Count the word only; do not judge whether an ablation was actually informative, what it established, or whether any necessity claim rests on it.

criteria.name: Checks whether a trivial approach would have sufficed
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract reports comparing against a deliberately trivial, naive, or degenerate alternative — random selection, the unmodified baseline, a no-op — in order to establish that the proposed machinery is needed at all. Score NA when no comparison of any kind is reported.

criteria.name: Methodological critique — a flawed practice in the field is named AND its consequence shown
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract identifies a specific defective practice in how the field evaluates, reports, or measures things, and separately whether it demonstrates what that defect costs (a wrong conclusion it produces, a method it falsely flatters); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low when a practice is criticised without demonstrated consequence.

criteria.name: Simplicity restoration — a simple or classical method is shown to match or beat elaborate recent ones
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how simple the method being advocated is (few parts, classical, little tuning, small code change), and separately how elaborate the approaches it is shown to match or beat are; score 0-10 for the CONTRAST. Score low when a simple method beats only other simple methods, and low when the advocated method is itself elaborate.

criteria.name: Efficiency-vocabulary density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses efficiency register — efficient, lightweight, scalable, fast, low-cost, cheap, practical, resource-friendly. Count the vocabulary only, not whether efficiency was actually achieved or measured.

criteria.name: Membership in the graph-learning / GNN subfield
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract belongs to the graph neural network, graph representation, or graph algorithms cluster. Score topic membership only; work of any quality in any other subfield scores 0.

criteria.name: Parenthetical example density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract inserts parenthetical examples or clarifications — '(e.g., ...)', '(such as ...)', '(i.e., ...)'. Count the parenthetical habit only.

criteria.name: Cost accounting includes the method's own overhead
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports a saving or speedup, and separately whether the accounting visibly includes what the method itself costs (its training, its extra passes, its added parameters); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for a headline speedup whose own overhead is not accounted for.

criteria.name: Reports the number a skeptic would ask for
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract volunteers the specific quantity most likely to undercut its own claim — the accuracy given up for a speedup, the failure rate, the gap remaining to a stronger method, the cost of the fix — rather than only the quantity that flatters it.

criteria.name: Includes a condition under which the method is expected to do badly
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the reported evaluation includes a setting chosen to stress or break the proposed approach — an adversarial case, an out-of-distribution regime, a condition the authors expect to be hard — as opposed to only favourable settings. Score NA when no evaluation is reported.

criteria.name: Unification — one mechanism handles problems previously treated separately
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how many genuinely distinct problems the abstract claims to address, and separately how single the mechanism addressing them is; score 0-10 for BOTH together — high when one clean mechanism covers several previously separate problems, low for a multi-part system covering several problems and low for one mechanism covering one problem.

criteria.name: Self-referential discourse markers
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how often the abstract refers to itself as a document — 'In this paper', 'In this work', 'Here we', 'This paper proposes'. Count the self-reference only.

criteria.name: The motivating observation is itself reported as a finding
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states an empirical observation that motivated the work, and separately whether that observation is presented as something the authors established rather than assumed or cited; score 0-10 for BOTH together.

criteria.name: Reports variability across seeds, splits, or runs
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract indicates that results were checked for stability across random seeds, data splits, or repeated runs — including reporting that instability was found. Score NA when the abstract reports no empirical results.

criteria.name: Mathematical symbols embedded in the method's own name
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the work's own method, benchmark, or dataset name contains mathematical or non-alphabetic symbols — Greek letters, subscripts, superscripts, exponents. Score the naming style only.

criteria.name: Credits what prior work got right while stating what it missed
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract acknowledges a genuine contribution of the work it builds on or displaces, and separately whether it states specifically what that work leaves unsolved; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for prior work described only as limited, and low for prior work praised with no gap identified.
